title: Finite orbit-coordinate realizers form a two-sided Cauchy net
statement: Let $G$ be a Hausdorff topological group whose identity has a basis of open subgroups. Let $\mathcal O_G$, $i_G$, $\omega_G$ and $F_G$ be the open-orbit category, its inclusion into discrete continuous left $G$-sets, and the two underlying-set functors [def-sfb-open-orbit-functor]. Give natural automorphism groups the pointwise topology [def-sfb-set-functor-aut-pointwise-topology]. Work in compatible universes. Fix $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(\omega_G)$ and put $D=\coprod_{U\text{ open}}G/U$, with elements tagged by their subgroup. There exists a family $(g_F)_{F\subseteq D\text{ finite}}$ in $G$, indexed by inclusion, such that $g_Fx=\alpha_U(x)$ for each tagged $x\in F\cap G/U$, including a choice for $F=\varnothing$. For each tagged $x\in G/U$ the set $C_x=\{g\in G:gx=\alpha_U(x)\}$ is a nonempty closed coset, and every finite intersection of these sets is nonempty, with the empty intersection equal to $G$. For every open subgroup $U$, if $F$ and $F\prime$ both contain the tagged coordinates $U\in G/U$ and $\alpha_U^{-1}(U)\in G/U$, then $g_F^{-1}g_{F\prime}\in U$ and $g_Fg_{F\prime}^{-1}\in U$. In particular this net is Cauchy for the two-sided uniformity: for every identity neighborhood $W$, both differences lie in $W$ for all sufficiently large $F,F\prime$.

proof.text: Fix a finite tagged set $F$. For each $x\in F\cap G/U_x$, choose $a_x\in G$ with $x=a_xU_x$ and put $H_x=a_xU_xa_x^{-1}$. The equation $hx=x$ is equivalent to $a_x^{-1}ha_x\in U_x$, so $H_x$ is its stabilizer. Conjugation and its inverse are continuous, hence $H_x$ is open. Put $V=\bigcap_{x\in F}H_x$, an open subgroup (take $V=G$ for $F=\varnothing$). By [def-sfb-open-orbit-functor], $G/V$ is an orbit object and $q_x:G/V\to G/U_x$, $hV\mapsto hx$, is an arrow: if $hV=kV$, then $k^{-1}h\in V\subseteq H_x$, so $hx=kx$; also $q_x(thV)=tq_x(hV)$.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.5, printed p. 64, projections from smaller open subgroups and the conjugate-orbit maps T_g; explicit common stabilizer for finite tagged coordinates.

proof.text: Apply naturality of $\alpha$ to each arrow $q_x$ of [def-sfb-open-orbit-functor]. Choose a representative $g\in G$ of the coset $\alpha_V(V)\in G/V$. Then $gx=q_x(gV)=q_x(\alpha_V(V))=\alpha_{U_x}(q_x(V))=\alpha_{U_x}(x)$ for every $x\in F$. Thus the set of realizers for each finite $F$ is nonempty. Choose one $g_F$ for each nonempty $F$, and set $g_{\varnothing}=1$. This gives the required family without imposing any compatibility between its choices.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.5, printed p. 64, compatibility of the automorphism with projection and conjugate-orbit maps; choosing representatives of its identity-coset values.

proof.text: For a coordinate $x$, step 2 with $F=\{x\}$ gives a realizer $r$. The equation $gx=rx$ is equivalent to $r^{-1}g\in H_x$, so $C_x=rH_x$. An open subgroup $H$ is closed: its complement is the union of the open cosets $bH$ for $b\notin H$, since distinct left cosets are disjoint. Translations are homeomorphisms, so $C_x$ is closed and nonempty. For a finite family of coordinates its intersection contains $g_F$ by step 2, and the empty intersection is $G$, containing $1$.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.5, printed p. 64, finite intersection property of prescribed-value cosets; closedness written out using open cosets.

proof.text: Fix an open subgroup $U$ and write $y=\alpha_U^{-1}(U)\in G/U$. If $F,F\prime$ contain both tagged coordinates $U,y$, put $a=g_F$ and $b=g_{F\prime}$. The prescriptions give $aU=\alpha_U(U)=bU$, hence $a^{-1}b\in U$. They also give $ay=\alpha_U(y)=U=by$. Applying $b^{-1}$ to $by=U$ yields $y=b^{-1}U$, and therefore $ab^{-1}U=ay=U$, hence $ab^{-1}\in U$. These computations use left cosets; $U$ need not be normal.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.5, printed p. 64, inverse-coordinate argument using hU=phi_U^{-1}(U) and the map T_h; two-sided finite-coordinate calculation.

proof.text: The finite subsets of $D$ form a directed set under inclusion: $F_1\cup F_2$ is an upper bound and $\varnothing$ is an index. Given an identity neighborhood $W$, choose an open subgroup $U\subseteq W$ by the assumed basis. Take $F_0=\{(U,U),(U,\alpha_U^{-1}(U))\}\subseteq D$. For every $F,F\prime\supseteq F_0$, step 4 puts both differences in $U\subseteq W$. This is exactly the two-sided Cauchy condition stated in the item; if the two tagged coordinates coincide, $F_0$ is simply a singleton.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.5, printed p. 64, Cauchy filter condition rewritten as the eventual condition for the directed set of finite tagged coordinates.
